title: Niantic / Pokemon GO / Keyhole -> Google geospatial lineage (John Hanke)
source: Public record: John Hanke founded Keyhole (In-Q-Tel-funded) -> Google acquired it 2004 (Google Earth/Maps); Hanke started Niantic Labs inside Google (2010), spun out 2015; Niantic shipped Ingress (2012) and Pokemon GO (2016) as real-world location/AR data collection; Niantic built a 'Large Geospatial Model' from player scans. Structural overlay; edges graded. Surveillance-cluster webbing (#217). NOTE: the In-Q-Tel tie is via Keyhole heritage only - no documented IQT funding of Niantic (do not imply one).

edges.notes: John Hanke co-founded Keyhole Inc. (the In-Q-Tel-funded geospatial startup) (fact).
Niantic Labs began inside Google (2010) and spun out as an independent company in 2015 (fact).
Ingress (2012) - Niantic's first location-based AR game, seeding its points-of-interest map (fact).
Pokemon GO (2016) - mass-scale location + real-world imagery/AR data collection via players (fact of data collection; downstream sharing/monetization contested).
Niantic remained tied to Google's maps/cloud ecosystem post-spinout; Google was also an investor (fact of relationship; exact data-flows not public).
